summary: The code-health feature itself looks right and fits the request. code_health.rs uses syn to measure each file's production lines (without #[cfg(test)] items) and its longest function, and joins landings and failure citations from the records. It applies the three thresholds and queues one 'Structural pass: <path>' request per breaching file, skipping any file that already has an open one. Every 10th landing it queues a self-contained, high-priority design review, with a baseline so existing history does not trigger one at once. It runs from both note_finished and land_pr, and athena status shows the table. Criteria 1–8 and 10 are met: 10 core tests, 2 hook tests (CLI integration tests, a file outside the deliverables list) and 1 display test all pass, and each asserts observed results. The verdict is still fail, because criterion 9 needs cargo test to pass and it does not on this tree. The one failure is binary.rs a_nested_run_works_in_a_scratch_copy_with_fake_agents, which stops on the sandbox's low-disk guard (9.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required). That looks environmental, not caused by the change, so a rerun with more free disk should pass. The rest are minor findings: the new test file is outside the deliverables list, the first-review baseline is a state file and not derived from records, and one table header is misaligned.
